page: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is an AMD-based general-purpose virtual machine provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz, providing 64 dedicated virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 256.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 3,780 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance is capable of attaching premium remote storage. No discrete GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core and compute capabilities, with stress-ng single-core execution and PassMark CPU ratings placing the instance in the top ten percent. Database operations on PassMark similarly reach the top decile, complemented by Redis SET benchmarks executing at 102.79 million operations per second and static web throughput reaching 72.71 GB/sec. Memory subsystems register 205.9 GB/sec read and 132.81 GB/sec write throughput on uncached 256 MB blocks. Hardware support for AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and AVX512_BF16 contributes to strong performance in data compression and small-to-medium parameter language model inference.

The bundled 3,780 GB NVMe SSD offers high-density local storage without the need for external network storage attachments for high-throughput scratch data. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of dedicated accelerators, which restricts execution speed on large 70-billion-parameter language models to average thresholds. Consequently, the instance is matched to high-concurrency relational and non-relational databases, Redis caching layers, ETL processing, software build pipelines, and enterprise application servers.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor within the Microsoft Hyper-V environment. It delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores at up to 4.5 GHz, paired with 256.0 GB of RAM in a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation. The hardware profile includes 3,780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports premium storage volumes, with no bundled GPU accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks reflect top-tier single-core CPU throughput, compression speeds, and database operations, alongside 102.79 million Redis operations per second and 72.71 GB/sec web serving throughput. Instruction support encompasses AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and bfloat16 vector formats. With its dense core configuration, robust memory bandwidth, and substantial onboard NVMe storage, this instance is suited for enterprise database hosting, memory caching clusters, CI/CD compilation, and high-traffic web applications.
